# FlareDragContext

`Flare.Components.FlareDragContext`

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Kind | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CanDrop` | `Func<TPayload?, string, bool>?` | `` | Parameter |  | Whether a payload may be dropped in a given target, asked once per drag for every zone declared as a FlareDropZone. A zone that says no never lights up and cannot receive the drop. Use it for what only the caller knows: a column is full, a card is locked. Accepts says the same thing per zone; both must agree. Zones a component declares as markup are NOT asked - the context cannot enumerate them, only the browser can. Refuse those by naming them in RefusedTargets. |
| `ChildContent` | `RenderFragment?` | `` | Parameter |  | The content that declares the draggables and drop zones. |
| `Group` | `string?` | `` | Parameter |  | Default group for the draggables and zones beneath this context. Items only see zones of their own group, so one context can hold two unrelated sets of things. |
| `KeyboardReorder` | `bool` | `true` | Parameter |  | Whether FlareDraggable items can be reordered from the keyboard: space picks one up, the arrows move it, space drops it, escape cancels. On by default - an item that only a pointer can move is a control half the readers cannot use. It makes every item a tab stop, which is right for a board and wrong for a list of a thousand; turn it off there and give the list its own roving focus. Items a host component renders itself (a data grid's rows, a tree's nodes) are not covered - their keys already mean something. |
| `OnDragEnd` | `EventCallback` | `` | Callback |  | Raised when a drag finishes, whether it landed or not - after OnDrop when it did. This is where a hint put up in OnDragStart comes down. |
| `OnDragStart` | `EventCallback<TPayload?>` | `` | Callback |  | Raised when an item is picked up, before it has moved anywhere. Free: the browser already asks which targets accept the item, and this rides on that call. |
| `OnDrop` | `EventCallback<FlareDropEventArgs<TPayload?>>` | `` | Callback |  | Raised once when a drag lands on a zone that accepted it. Not raised when the drop was cancelled, dropped on nothing, or dropped back onto the item itself. |
| `RefusedTargets` | `Func<TPayload?, IEnumerable<string>>?` | `` | Parameter |  | Zones that must not take the payload, named by id, asked once per drag. This is the answer for a component that declares its zones as markup rather than as FlareDropZone components: the context has no list of those to run CanDrop over, so it takes a refusal instead. A tree refusing its own subtree is the case this exists for - the branches inside a dragged node belong to it, and a drop there detaches the whole branch from the tree. |
| `ResolveItem` | `DragItemResolver<TPayload?>?` | `` | Parameter |  | Resolves an id to its payload for items that are NOT FlareDraggable components - a data grid's tr, a tree's li, anything that cannot take a wrapper element without producing invalid markup. Such an element carries the model's data attributes itself and this answers for it. Consulted only when no registered draggable owns the id. SourceTargetId is null for these, since there is no component to have been declared inside a zone. |
| `AdditionalAttributes` | `IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object>?` | `` | Parameter |  | Additional attributes. Inherited from `FlareComponentBase`. |
| `Class` | `string?` | `` | Parameter |  | Additional CSS class(es) appended to the component's root element. Inherited from `FlareComponentBase`. |
| `Style` | `string?` | `` | Parameter |  | Inline style string appended to the component's root element. Inherited from `FlareComponentBase`. |

## Methods

### `DisposeAsync()`

Detaches the context's pointer gesture.
Returns: `ValueTask`.

### `OnDragEndAsync()`

Reports that a drag finished. Called by the browser once per drag, landed or not.
Returns: `Task`.

### `OnDragStartAsync(string sourceId)`

Which zones will take the item that has just been picked up. Called by the browser once per drag; null means every zone in the item's group, which is the common case and saves marshalling a list that says the same thing.
Returns: `Task<DragTargetRuling>`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sourceId` | `string` | The dragged item's id. |

### `OnDropAsync(string sourceId, string targetId, int index, string edge, string overId)`

Reports where a drag landed. Called by the browser once per completed drop.
Returns: `Task`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sourceId` | `string` | The dragged item's id. |
| `targetId` | `string` | The zone the drop landed in. |
| `index` | `int` | The position the item takes, counted without the dragged item; -1 when the drop was into a zone or onto an item rather than between items. |
| `edge` | `string` | Where the drop landed relative to the item under the pointer. |
| `overId` | `string` | The id of the item under the pointer, when there was one. |
